html:
Degania, now Degania Alef, is a farming commune at the south end of the Sea of Galilee, founded in 1910 by young Jewish settlers in Ottoman Palestine. It is called the mother of all kibbutzim.

A group of about a dozen pioneers, most from the Russian Empire, settled land bought by the Jewish National Fund. They held all property in common, shared work and meals, and ran the farm by general meeting. Children were later raised partly in communal children's houses.

The model spread. Hundreds of kibbutzim followed, and they set the borders of Jewish settlement, trained fighters and supplied many leaders, among them Ben-Gurion's Labour movement. The Hebrew poet Rachel lived at Degania, and Moshe Dayan was born there.

In May 1948, in the first Arab-Israeli war, Degania's defenders stopped a Syrian advance at the gate. In later decades most kibbutzim, Degania among them, moved toward private pay and industry. See also the National Water Carrier, which draws from the same lake, and the wider movement of Zionism.
sum: Degania, now Degania Alef, is a farming commune at the south end of the Sea of Galilee, founded in 1910 by young Jewish settlers in Ottoman Palestine. It is called the mother of all kibbutzim.
